mcqs.question: Which of the following statements correctly compares a compound with a mixture?

options.A: A compound has a fixed ratio of elements, while a mixture can have varying proportions of its components.
options.B: A compound can be separated by simple filtration, whereas a mixture cannot.
options.C: Compounds are always solids, while mixtures are always liquids.
options.D: Compounds consist of only one type of atom, whereas mixtures consist of different atoms.

mcqs.answer: A compound has a fixed ratio of elements, while a mixture can have varying proportions of its components.
mcqs.explanation: Compounds are formed when elements combine in a definite, fixed proportion (e.g., H₂O always has two H atoms for each O atom). In a mixture the components retain their individual identities and can be present in any proportion, so the ratio is not fixed. Options B, C and D are incorrect because they state false properties of compounds and mixtures.

mcqs.question: A student discovers a pure substance that cannot be broken down into simpler substances by any chemical reaction. Which definition best describes this substance?

options.A: A substance made of two or more elements chemically combined in a fixed proportion.
options.B: A substance consisting of only one type of atom, which cannot be chemically broken down further.
options.C: A combination of substances that can be separated by physical means.
options.D: A material that changes its composition when heated.

mcqs.answer: A substance consisting of only one type of atom, which cannot be chemically broken down further.
mcqs.explanation: An element is a pure substance made of only one kind of atom and cannot be chemically decomposed into simpler substances. Option A describes a compound, C describes a mixture, and D is unrelated to the definition of an element.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about compounds is correct?

options.A: Compounds are formed when two or more elements are physically mixed together.
options.B: Compounds consist of two or more elements chemically combined in a definite proportion.
options.C: Compounds can be separated into their constituent elements by simple sieving.
options.D: Compounds have the same properties as the elements that form them.

mcqs.answer: Compounds consist of two or more elements chemically combined in a definite proportion.
mcqs.explanation: A compound results from a chemical combination of elements in a fixed ratio, giving it properties different from its constituent elements. Option A confuses mixtures with compounds, C suggests a physical method that cannot break chemical bonds, and D is false because compounds have distinct properties.

mcqs.question: Which reasoning correctly distinguishes an element from a compound?

options.A: Elements can be broken down into simpler substances by physical methods, compounds cannot.
options.B: Elements consist of identical atoms, whereas compounds consist of different atoms chemically combined.
options.C: Elements always exist as gases, while compounds always exist as liquids.
options.D: Both elements and compounds have variable composition.

mcqs.answer: Elements consist of identical atoms, whereas compounds consist of different atoms chemically combined.
mcqs.explanation: Elements are made of only one type of atom; compounds contain two or more different atoms chemically bonded in a fixed ratio. Option A is wrong because elements cannot be broken down chemically, C is incorrect as elements and compounds can be solids, liquids, or gases, and D misstates the fixed composition of compounds.

mcqs.learning_point: Recognise that compounds have fixed composition
mcqs.question: Which pair of statements correctly illustrates that compounds have a fixed composition while mixtures do not?

options.A: Water (H₂O) always contains hydrogen and oxygen in a 2:1 atom ratio, whereas air can have varying amounts of nitrogen and oxygen.
options.B: Table salt can be separated by a magnet, while sand cannot be separated by any method.
options.C: Carbon dioxide can be broken into carbon and oxygen by heating, while a sugar solution cannot be separated.
options.D: All compounds are solids, and all mixtures are liquids.

mcqs.answer: Water (H₂O) always contains hydrogen and oxygen in a 2:1 atom ratio, whereas air can have varying amounts of nitrogen and oxygen.
mcqs.explanation: In a compound like water, the ratio of H to O atoms is always 2:1, showing fixed composition. Air is a mixture of gases where the proportion of nitrogen, oxygen, etc., can vary. Options B, C, and D contain factual errors about separation methods, chemical decomposition, and physical states.

mcqs.question: In a competitive exam, which of the following is a true distinction between a compound and a mixture?

options.A: Compounds have uniform composition throughout, whereas mixtures may have non‑uniform composition.
options.B: Compounds can be separated by filtration, whereas mixtures cannot be separated by any physical method.
options.C: Compounds are always inorganic, while mixtures are always organic.
options.D: Compounds consist of only one element, whereas mixtures consist of two or more elements.

mcqs.answer: Compounds have uniform composition throughout, whereas mixtures may have non‑uniform composition.
mcqs.explanation: A compound is a pure substance with the same composition everywhere. A mixture can have varying composition in different parts. Options B, C, and D are incorrect: compounds generally cannot be separated by simple filtration, the inorganic/organic distinction is unrelated, and compounds are made of more than one element.

mcqs.question: An element is best defined as:

options.A: A pure substance that consists of only one kind of atom.
options.B: A substance formed by chemically combining two or more elements.
options.C: A mixture of different substances that can be separated physically.
options.D: A material that can be broken down into simpler substances by heating.

mcqs.answer: A pure substance that consists of only one kind of atom.
mcqs.explanation: Elements are pure substances made up of a single type of atom and cannot be chemically broken down further. Option B describes a compound, C describes a mixture, and D is incorrect because heating does not decompose an element into simpler substances.

mcqs.question: A compound can be defined as:

options.A: A pure substance composed of two or more different elements chemically combined in a fixed proportion.
options.B: A mixture of substances that can be separated by filtration.
options.C: A single type of atom that cannot be broken down further.
options.D: A collection of identical molecules that are not chemically bonded.

mcqs.answer: A pure substance composed of two or more different elements chemically combined in a fixed proportion.
mcqs.explanation: Compounds consist of two or more elements chemically bonded in definite ratios, giving them unique properties. Option B describes a mixture, C describes an element, and D misstates the nature of chemical bonding in compounds.
